symptom.result: The original two-file baseline reproduced at 65 passed / 8 failed. After contract reconciliation, the full KernelOne audit scope passes 597 tests.
resolved_failures: Seven failures were stale duplicate-test expectations: persisted audit restoration intentionally requires the complete signed envelope, and audit writes/queries intentionally require a valid non-empty run_id.

One production inconsistency was real: normalize_event_type silently mapped empty input to task_start, allowing missing event identity to be misclassified. Empty input now fails closed through KernelAuditEventType validation.

scope_separation.evidence: The 65-passed/8-failed baseline was reproduced before this dedicated bucket changed any audit source or tests, proving separation from the earlier ContextOS work. This bucket intentionally changes validators.py plus the stale contract/validator tests; contracts.py remains unchanged. Focused, full-audit, and release-gate commands independently validate that narrow diff.

authoritative_evidence: Commit 700c09cc (Validate persisted audit event chains) intentionally made every persisted envelope field mandatory and added canonical strict unit tests.
require_valid_run_id has been fail-closed since its original implementation and all runtime emit/query callers consume that strict contract.
The only split-brain was normalize_event_type: one suite required rejection while a duplicate unit test preserved the silent task_start default.

bench_impact: Pre-bench static/test gate cannot be declared globally clean until the intended audit contract is identified and implementation/tests are reconciled without weakening fail-closed semantics.
